Analysis is the study of limits, and of the operations that survive
them: derivatives, integrals, infinite sums. The three galleries
below, from [@eeanimation](https://www.instagram.com/eeanimation/),
are the introduction to this page: branches of the subject, the
standard calculus theorems, then complex analysis in more detail.

## Branches of mathematical analysis {#sec-intro}

Real analysis builds the foundations. Complex analysis studies
functions of $z = x+iy$. Functional analysis moves to infinite
dimensions; harmonic analysis reads frequency; numerical and
asymptotic analysis approximate; variational and nonlinear analysis
handle extrema and $F(x)=0$.

[23 August 2026](https://www.instagram.com/p/DcZTXr4AVcB/).

## Calculus theorems {#sec-theorems}

A useful habit: every interchange of a limit and an operation is a
theorem. The series runs from the squeeze theorem through the
divergence theorem — hypotheses first, formula second.

[12 September 2026](https://www.instagram.com/p/DdMuCr1DyUs/).

{{< include ../_includes/galleries/DdMuCr1DyUs.qmd >}}

## Complex analysis {#sec-complex}

A function $f:\Omega\subset\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ is **holomorphic**
if it is complex-differentiable on an open set. That single
requirement is much stronger than real differentiability in two
variables: Cauchy–Riemann, power series, contour integrals,
residues, conformal maps.

## Bridges to the rest of the site {#sec-bridges}

- Linear ODEs with constant coefficients are solved by
  characteristic polynomials — that is
  [linear algebra](../linear-algebra/matrix-decompositions.qmd)
  over $\mathbb C$.
- Generating functions and characteristic functions in
  [probability](../statistics/probability.qmd) are analytic
  objects first, probabilistic ones second.
- Hamilton–Jacobi theory on the
  [dynamics page](../dynamics/differential-equations.qmd) is a
  first-order nonlinear PDE.
